title: Artificial intelligence-assisted identification and quantification of osteoclasts
author: Emmanuel, Brüel, et al.

steps.title: Animal sacrifice and tissue fixation
steps.instruction: Euthanize female Wistar rats with an intraperitoneal overdose of 200 mg kg⁻¹ pentobarbital (Mebumal) while under 4 % isoflurane inhalation anesthesia, immediately excise right tibiae, and immersion‑fix them in 0.1 M sodium‑phosphate‑buffered 4 % formaldehyde (pH 7.0) for 48 h, then transfer to 70 % ethanol.

steps.title: Embedding, sectioning, and staining
steps.instruction: For the first cohort (ten 20‑week‑old rats) embed tibiae undecalcified in methyl methacrylate (MMA), cut 7‑µm sections with a Jung RM2065 microtome, and stain for TRAP using pararosaniline base (Sigma‑Aldrich P7632) followed by aniline‑blue counterstain. For the second cohort (ten 18–20‑week‑old rats) decalcify tibiae in formic acid, embed in paraffin, cut 7‑µm sections, and stain for cathepsin K with polyclonal rabbit anti‑cathepsin K antibody (AP08851PU‑N, Acris) at 1:200 dilution.

steps.title: Image acquisition via slide scanner
steps.instruction: Scan the stained sections with a Hamamatsu NanoZoomer 2.0‑HT digital slide scanner (or view live images on a Nikon Eclipse i80 bright‑field microscope equipped with an Olympus DP70 camera for manual counting). Use Visiopharm VIS (v. 2019.12 or newer) for subsequent image analysis.

steps.title: Annotate region of interest in VIS
steps.instruction: In Visiopharm VIS, right‑click (or press F5) to activate Annotate, draw a Poly Line along the distal growth‑plate of the proximal tibial metaphysis, measure a point 1500 µm (rats) or 300 µm (mice) below this line (hotkey F2), copy the line and paste it at the measured distance, then paste a second line 3000 µm (rats) or 1000 µm (mice) below the first. Use the ROI Drawing tool (hotkey F4) to draw a polygon or freehand ROI following these lines, delineating the endosteal bone surface to include only trabecular bone. Delete the annotation lines if desired.

steps.title: Create bone classifier app
steps.instruction: Within the same image, create a new app (New App → New Class), label two classes: Background (green) and Bone (blue). Open the Classification tab, select Deep Learning with the default U‑Net model, keep all other settings at default, and choose 20× (preferred) or 10× magnification. Add the previously drawn ROI under Regions To Analyze, press Train, and run at least 10 000 iterations (up to 100 000 recommended). Preview the result; if bone is mis‑classified, repeat ROI labeling and retrain. Add post‑processing steps: Outline As ROI for Background → ROIBackground, Outline As ROI for Bone → ROIBone, then a Close operation of 10–40 µm to smooth the bone‑background interface (optional Change by Shape). Rename the bone ROI to ROIBone, load the slide into the Slide Tray, and Run the app. Perform visual inspection and manually correct obvious mis‑classifications.

steps.title: Create osteoclast classifier app
steps.instruction: Repeat the ROI‑labeling and app‑creation workflow (steps G–O) using the same image: label a third class ‘Osteoclasts’ (red) instead of Bone, create a new app, and train with the same Deep Learning U‑Net settings. Replace any reference to ROIBackground with ROIBone where appropriate. After training, add a new Output Variable (New Variable) to store the osteoclast surface measurement.

steps.title: Calculate osteoclast surface ratio
steps.instruction: Define Bone Surface (BS) as the length of the interface between ROIBone and ROIBackground, define Osteoclast Surface (Oc.S) as the length of the interface between the osteoclast area and ROIBone, and compute the ratio Oc.S / BS as the final output variable.
